facts.fact: The Ministry of ICT and National Guidance Q4 FY2021/22 report states National ICT Policy drafting was completed and awaiting presentation to and approval by Cabinet; the output, first titled National Digital Transformation Policy, was retitled National ICT Policy per the Cabinet Secretariat.

The report shows the Ministry of ICT and National Guidance (E-Services department, Enabling Policies output) running the National ICT Policy's regulatory impact assessment, drafting and Cabinet submission.

The report shows UShs 249.775 million spent by the E-Services department on the output covering the National ICT Policy and the National Cyber Security Strategy (wage UShs 177.025 million, non-wage UShs 72.75 million), in a GoU vote; the spend is shared by both outputs.

facts.fact: The Ministry of Finance's FY2022/23 Digital Transformation Programme monitoring report states stakeholder engagement for the National ICT Policy was finalised, pending submission to the Cabinet Secretariat.

The document is a Final Draft National ICT Policy dated May 2022, prepared by a consultant for the Ministry of ICT and National Guidance and signed in a foreword by the Minister; it states no adoption.
The draft lists the National ICT Policy 2014 among the key policies of the ICT sector's current policy environment, which the draft revises.
The full text of the final draft is available online on the consultant's website; it is a draft, and the document gives no official publication.
The draft contains no implementation or action plan; it states the Ministry will develop a road map informing a monitoring and evaluation framework and implementation matrix.

The draft makes the Ministry of ICT and National Guidance responsible for policy guidance, oversight, and leading adoption, implementation, monitoring and evaluation, working with the Digital Transformation Programme Working Group.
The draft states no budget, cost or funding source for the policy.
